method: The first three anchors were frozen from titles/metadata before inspecting their source bodies; graph snapshot node descriptions and explicit graph edges were then inspected, followed by live original GitHub issue states/bodies/comments and relevant links. Same reviewer saw both; no blinded decision quality or equal-time retrieval comparison. No code was run on HPC.

cases.minimum_action: Use existing queue, node-failure, retry and restart logs for a small cost/latency decision table; compare spare-node and ordinary requeue scenarios before touching integration code.
cases.stop_condition: If queued restart is fast/reliable enough or no representative logs are available, no further implementation.

overall_finding: For these three locked anchors, project decisions materially depend on public comment evidence not present in the bounded graph snapshot; a conventional issue+comments read finds them. A source-backed on-demand comment packet can close this coverage gap without collecting all comments or asserting semantic links.
next_gate: Run an independently assessed, equal-source reviewer decision test (or use practical maintainer feedback) before claiming graph superiority or expanding research-agent infrastructure.
